item4.title: winner lock-in at a fixed prediction horizon
item4.estimand: P(the branch that is the winner at time t is still the winner at t + Delta), as a function of the winner margin at time t
item4.pooling_forbidden: horizons are never pooled into the primary statistic

definitions.winner_at_t: argmax of the smoothed branch probability at t
definitions.margin_at_t: top-1 minus top-2 smoothed probability at t
definitions.outcome: 1 if the winner at t + Delta equals the winner at t, else 0

item4.data: canonical 1024-rollout Track D trajectories; features taken only at t
item4.leakage_rule: no future information may enter preprocessing, filtering, imputation, normalisation or feature selection; standardisation is fitted on training folds only

inclusion_and_ties.include: every (question, continuation, t) cell where both t and t + Delta exist
inclusion_and_ties.tie_definition: margin <= 1e-9 counts as a tie at t
inclusion_and_ties.primary_handling: ties retained, outcome decided by argmax as implemented
inclusion_and_ties.sensitivity: repeat excluding ties, and excluding near-ties with margin < 0.01

bootstrap.method: question-cluster bootstrap retaining all continuation and time observations of a resampled question

baselines: margin plus time and continuation controls

metrics: logistic coefficient and odds ratio for margin with clustered CI
calibration: reliability table and Brier score
performance by margin quantile with denominators
item4.model_comparison: bootstrap the PAIRED metric difference on the same resampled questions; never infer improvement from separate CIs
item4.decision_rule: the pooled AUROC 0.872 [0.852, 0.892] stays labelled DESCRIPTIVE. It may be replaced in the paper only if the fixed-horizon, question-clustered estimate is positive, its CI excludes the null, and the direction is robust to the declared tie handling and to the controls.
item4.naming_rule: this tests winner PERSISTENCE / LOCK-IN. It must not be described as predicting future instability.
